title: Lahaina Disaster Recovery Update Meeting: March 13, 2024

recap.headline: Lahaina debris cleanup, water and sewer testing, and landfill land vote update
recap.in_60_seconds: Maui County held its weekly Lahaina disaster recovery meeting with Mayor Bissen, Councilmember Paltin, the Army Corps of Engineers and the EPA. The Army Corps said 306 fire-damaged properties have been cleared of debris, and the EPA said sewer line inspections are done and water main testing is nearly finished. Councilmember Paltin said a resolution to take Central Maui landfill land by eminent domain fell one vote short at five of six needed, with more discussion March 19 and a new vote March 22. About 14 residents asked questions, mostly about the gravel left on cleared lots, rebuilding timelines, water and sewer restoration, and the eminent domain plan. Some questions were left open, including FEMA housing eligibility for people with past convictions and whether water meters can be permitted before building permits.

parts.title: Welcome and announcements
presented: The Army Corps would update debris cleanup, followed by open questions.
A meeting is aimed for April 16, including staff of the new expedited permitting office under the Office of Recovery.
A temporary housing resource event is set for March 16 and 23 at 9 a.m. at the Westin Maui in Kāʻanapali.

next.what: Temporary housing resource event at the Westin Maui, Kāʻanapali
Community meeting with expedited permitting office staff

parts.title: Mayor's remarks
presented: The Mayor thanked residents for coming back to the weekly Wednesday meetings.
A Department of Human Services representative came from Oʻahu to take questions.

parts.title: Councilmember update on landfill eminent domain and Lahaina bypass
presented: A resolution to acquire Central Maui landfill land by eminent domain got 5 votes; 6 were needed.
Four councilmembers voted no; the Councilmember said the delay is about two weeks at best.
The resolution comes back for discussion and testimony March 19 at 1:30 p.m., with a vote March 22 needing six yes votes.
The Maui MPO policy board will take up the status of the northern portion of the Lahaina bypass, and testimony is welcome.

next.what: Council committee discussion and testimony on landfill eminent domain, no vote
First Council vote on the eminent domain resolution
Councilmember to post meeting details on social media

parts.title: Army Corps debris removal update
parts.presenter: Army Corps of Engineers debris mission commander
presented: 306 properties are cleared of debris, just under 20% of properties, in under 60 days.
76 rights-of-entry were returned to the County; about 173 properties are deferred due to overhead hazards or heavy metals.
Deferred properties with a signed right-of-entry will get a call and a safety step before going on the cleanup schedule, with calls 3 days and 24 hours ahead.

next.what: Undeferral process posted on the website

parts.title: EPA sewer and water sampling update
presented: EPA finished sewer line camera inspections; lines it could not reach were passed to the Department of Environmental Management.
Hydrant sampling of water mains is nearly done; cultural monitors are being hired for sensitive areas.
Sampling of laterals to each property comes next and will take some weeks, starting where standing homes lack water service.
The County's MauiRecovers.org site remains the authority on whether water is safe; a call center runs Monday to Saturday, 7 a.m. to 7 p.m.

next.what: Sampling of water laterals, starting in areas with standing structures

parts.title: Questions on sewer, eminent domain and gravel

raised.concern: What the sewer survey found and what the next step is to make sewer lines work again.
Whether condemning the landfill land would set a precedent for eminent domain in Lahaina.
Gravel spread on cleared lots will cost uninsured owners to remove; residents suggested plastic sheeting, burlap, or reusing the gravel elsewhere.
Whether a past felony conviction keeps people out of FEMA direct lease or other FEMA housing.
Whether a lot that fails soil testing goes to the back of the line for another scrape.

answered.said: The Department of Environmental Management is evaluating the sewer findings; EPA's work sped things up, but EPA cannot speak for the County on next steps.
A state bill, SB 3381, would remove that authority from counties but is undecided; land can only be taken for a public purpose.
Each case stands on its own; this is a used quarry needed for 400,000 tons of debris, and the owner wants far more than the appraised value, so it is not a precedent for other land.
Gravel keeps soil on lots that may sit for a long time; removing old foundations was meant to offset the cost.
Hydroseeding did not work in Lahaina's climate; the Mayor invited other ideas such as staked plastic.
Burlap works with seeding and sprinklers, which Lahaina lots cannot support without water lines.
Rescraping crews handle failed lots; passing lots get a closeout affidavit sent to the County and the owner is notified.

parts.title: Questions on water testing, rebuilding and staffing

raised.concern: Why water sampling takes so long, and whether funding could set up a lab on Maui.
Whether the water meter goes back on once a lateral passes testing.
How long owners wait to rebuild, whether Wahikuli gets underground power, heavy traffic, and a request for the Planning Department to attend.
Asking the state senator to explain SB 3381 at the April 16 meeting.
Getting a water meter permit before a building permit so lots can be irrigated instead of graveled.
Speeding lateral sampling with certified staff from other islands and more federal funding.
What happens if an owner who wants to be present is off island when the 72-hour notice comes.

answered.said: Shipping is not the slow part; lab tests take about two weeks for final results, with preliminary results sooner, and a local lab would take longer to set up.
The valve is closed and meter box protected; the meter will likely be replaced when the home is rebuilt.
With 21 crews working and sewer and water not yet cleared, no timeline is set; neighborhood meetings will give a better idea, and an expedited permitting process is being set up.
Neighborhood meetings are scheduled, including April 20 at 3 p.m. for one mauka neighborhood, with an online option being planned.
They will ask the senator to come; the administration does not support the bill.
He did not know and referred it to the Department of Water Supply; the host will add it to the homeowners meeting.
Sampling is limited to about 200 properties a week by County staff and copper sampling equipment.
He will ask two other mayors tomorrow for staff, and the County asks federal partners for funding all the time.
It is case by case; owners can be moved later in the order, and can call the hotline if a contractor says no.

parts.title: Closing announcements
presented: The Mayor's State of the County Address is this Friday at the Maui Arts and Cultural Center's Castle Theater, doors at 5 p.m.
It will air live on Akaka and the County's Facebook page.
